answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. The upshot is a network where trust is a resource you earn, not a quantity you can mint — and that is what keeps Sybil attacks economically unviable. Consider a forge as the anchor of the cost.
